title: Kth Largest Element
summary: Return the k-th largest value without fully sorting the array.
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the **k-th largest** element: the element that would be at position k if the array were sorted in descending order. Duplicates count separately, so in `[3, 3, 1]` the 2nd largest is 3.

Try to do better than sorting the whole array.
hints: Sorting everything works in O(n log n), but you only care about the top k values. As you read the numbers one by one, what's the least you need to remember?
Keep a min-heap (PriorityQueue) of size k holding the k largest values seen so far. When it grows past k, remove its smallest element. At the end, the smallest value in the heap is the k-th largest.

Sorting costs O(n log n). A size-k min-heap keeps exactly the top k values: anything smaller than the heap's minimum can't be in the top k, and the minimum itself is the k-th largest. Each of n insertions costs O(log k), so O(n log k) time and O(k) space, which is much better when k is small. (Quickselect averages O(n) but is O(n^2) in the worst case.)
